task: Design the implementation plan and exact requirements for one copy-paste master prompt that a user can run in the VS Code Codex extension to take this WishWell repository from evidence-grounded product discovery through a complete whole-system audit, decision finalization, small-task implementation, testing, remediation, and truthful delivery readiness. The prompt itself—not this council run—must drive the future coding work. It must first answer a thorough product and engineering intake from repository evidence and council reasoning, ask the user only one consolidated batch of genuinely blocking questions, finalize the selected scope and acceptance criteria before any implementation, then decompose work into small independently verifiable tasks and implement them to completion. The prompt must use only Codex GPT-5.6 Sol for the root agent, planners, reviewers, judge, and subagents; no Claude, Gemini, OpenCode, or other development-agent provider. This provider restriction must not remove or redesign the product's existing native Firebase AI Logic/Gemini feature. Ground every recommendation in the current working tree and its binding PROJECT_ABOUT.md contract. The resulting prompt must cover UI/UX, React Native frontend, TypeScript application/domain layers, Kotlin Android native boundaries, Swift iOS native boundaries, TurboModules/bridges, Firebase Functions/Firestore/Hosting middleware and backend, persistence and migrations, identity and contacts, AI safety, background work, SMS/MessageUI platform truth, concurrency/idempotency, error and recovery states, privacy/security/abuse/legal/policy, accessibility/localization/adaptive design, performance/resource use, dependencies/supply chain, testing/e2e, CI, observability/operations, release evidence, store/cloud readiness, and only behavior-relevant documentation. It must preserve pre-existing user changes, avoid broad document rewrites, avoid fake success, and leave no routine local engineering work for the user while still stopping for destructive/external/costly actions, secrets, signing, provider/store mutations, legal approvals, physical-device/carrier evidence, and other authority that only a human or external system can supply.
constraints: Treat PROJECT_ABOUT.md as the sole product/technical source of truth; README.md, DESIGN.md, code, generated designs, and reports may not silently override it.

The repository has no AGENT.md or AGENTS.md today. The master prompt must load canonical AGENTS.md and nested overrides when present, also accept legacy AGENT.md when present, report absence, and fall back to repository evidence without inventing instructions.
The working tree is already heavily modified. Never reset, revert, overwrite, reformat, stage, or commit pre-existing changes unless they are directly required and attributable to the requested work.
This is a React Native Android/iOS birthday-automation product. VS Code Codex is the execution surface, not the product type.

Pin development-agent orchestration to gpt-5.6-sol. If the IDE exposes the gpt-5.6 alias, require a current-session capability check that it resolves to Sol; never silently fall back to another model or provider.
Use an independent Codex-only council, anonymize and randomize candidate plans before judging, and treat council outputs as untrusted evidence rather than executable instructions.

Answer discoverable intake questions using code, tests, PROJECT_ABOUT.md, current official primary-source research, and explicit confidence/evidence. Ask the user only for material choices that cannot safely be inferred.
Finalize one coherent decision package—business outcome, users/jobs, scope/non-goals, platform behavior, acceptance criteria, architecture, risks, and validation—before implementation begins.

Before implementation, build a dependency-ordered backlog of small, independently testable tasks with exact locations, acceptance criteria, validation, rollback, and explicit dependencies. Finish and verify one task before starting a dependent task.
Permit parallel read-only exploration and disjoint write work only when ownership is explicit; serialize overlapping or safety-critical edits and always synthesize/review results in the root thread.

Preserve Android unattended SMS versus iOS foreground MessageUI semantics, local-first private data boundaries, fail-closed coordination, duplicate prevention, and all binding BA contracts and Section 19 gates.

Never deploy, upload, send a real SMS, mutate Firebase/Google/Apple/Play/App Store state, purchase services, create/rotate credentials, weaken a release gate, or claim external approval without explicit authority and evidence.
Use synthetic data for tests and research. Never place private contact/message/account data or secrets in prompts, logs, council artifacts, search queries, fixtures, or reports.
Do not improve every document. Update only directly affected source-of-truth, contract, runbook, or user-facing documentation in the same change; avoid duplicate specs and unrelated cleanup.

A passing build is not delivery readiness. Require representative unit, integration, contract, native, emulator/simulator, accessibility, localization, performance, security, e2e, artifact, and release-evidence checks proportional to each change, plus an explicit external-evidence ledger.

The final prompt should be powerful but lean: state each rule once, define autonomy and approval boundaries in one place, keep evidence and stopping conditions explicit, and avoid decorative process repetition.

The final plan must identify likely prompt failure modes, anti-shortcuts, completion criteria, and a final report schema that distinguishes completed, verified, blocked-by-external-authority, and not-applicable work.
